source_units.text: The smart greenhouse operation system consists of a greenhouse management server (GMS), 2 heating boilers, a thermal curtain unit, 30 environmental sensors, and a nutrient solution supplier. The environmental sensors measure temperature, humidity, and CO2 concentration.
Externally, there are the meteorological agency forecast service and the power company; the cultivation manager handles equipment operation, and the equipment technician handles equipment repair.

At 10:00 p.m., the GMS receives a forecast of an early-morning minimum temperature of -12 °C from the meteorological agency forecast service. If the forecast temperature is -10 °C or less, the GMS issues the cold-wave alert mode. The GMS issues the cold-wave alert mode and sends a notification to the cultivation manager.
In the cold-wave alert mode, the thermal curtain unit closes the thermal curtain, and Boiler 1 maintains the greenhouse target temperature at 15 °C. The two measures start simultaneously.
The environmental sensors measure the indoor temperature every 10 min and transmit it to the GMS. If the indoor temperature drops below 12 °C, the GMS additionally operates Boiler 2.
At 2:00 a.m., when the environmental sensors measure an indoor temperature of 11.5 °C, the GMS operates Boiler 2.
At 3:00 a.m., Boiler 1 stops due to a combustion failure. The GMS detects the Boiler 1 stop and requests an emergency dispatch from the equipment technician.
After arriving, the equipment technician inspects the ignition device and replaces the clogged fuel filter. When the filter replacement is finished, the equipment technician reignites Boiler 1.
Until Boiler 1 is reignited, the cultivation manager stops the nutrient solution supply. This is because a low nutrient solution temperature causes root damage.
At 4:20 a.m., when Boiler 1 is reignited and the indoor temperature recovers to 15 °C, the cultivation manager resumes the nutrient solution supply.
At 7:00 a.m., when the outdoor temperature rises to -5 °C or more, the GMS releases the cold-wave alert mode and stops Boiler 2.
If the indoor humidity is 90% or more, the cultivation manager opens the vent window for 5 min. On this day, the humidity stayed at 85%, so the vent window was not opened.
The goal of this scenario is to maintain the indoor temperature at 12 °C or more without crop frost damage.
